subproblems.title: Mass formula and support of an integer multiplicity current (Simon 6.3.2(3), 6.2.12)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep: M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, equal to ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Let μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then (i) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (ii) spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support
subproblems.natural_proof:

- Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above, so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node.
- It is also already a frozen dependency of the selected node.
- Use in the selected node:
  * The parent assembly (supplied step 1) uses spt X = ℝ^P ∩ spt μ_R, which with Measure.measure_compl_support gives μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ spt X) = 0.
  * Sibling support_closed (its step 3) uses spt Y = ℝ^P ∩ spt μ_R for its triple R. The parent applies it to the pushed-forward triple R'.

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–765: M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for open W) and Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12 (chapter-06.txt lines 295–307: spt T = spt μ_T). The book states both without proof; a complete proof follows. Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. For an n-covector α, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm; I runs over strictly increasing multi-indices, e_I = (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})), and dx^I denotes the coordinate covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}. ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ means ξ(x)(α).
1. Pointwise algebra. Let x ∈ M be a point where R.orients holds: there are an orthonormal family τ₁, …, τₙ and s ∈ {1, −1} with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every α. Expanding τ_j = Σ_i τ_j^i e_i, multilinearity and alternation give α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where det(τ^I) is the n×n minor of the matrix (τ_j^i) on the rows I; by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α. The covector ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩ dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), hence |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 and ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1. (For n = 0 the only I is empty: |α| = |α()|, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1.) Since R.orients holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M and μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, these facts hold μ_R-a.e. The field x ↦ ξ^♭(x) is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable, being a continuous linear function of the a.e. strongly measurable ξ (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. Integral formula. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: it is a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off the compact set spt ω ⊆ U, is bounded by θ·sup|ω| a.e. (step 1), and ∫_{M∩spt ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Hence T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R (integral with respect to the density θ).
3. Upper bound. Let W be open and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). By step 1, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for μ_R-a.e. x, and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W) by step 2. Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
4. Lower bound. Let W be open and t a real number with t < μ_R(W); we construct an admissible ω with T(ω) > t, which proves M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Put G := W ∩ U (open). Since M ⊆ U, μ_R(G) = μ_R(W). μ_R is a Borel measure, finite on compact subsets of U; restricted to the open σ-compact set G it is a Radon measure (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15), hence inner regular by compact sets and outer regular on sets of finite measure. Fix η > 0 and a compact K ⊆ G with μ_R(K) > t + 4η. (a) Lusin (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17): there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that ξ^♭ restricted to K' is continuous, and |ξ^♭| = 1, ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ = 1 μ_R-a.e. on K'. (b) There is an open V with K' ⊆ V, V̄ compact, V̄ ⊆ G, and μ_R(V ∖ K') < η. (c) Extend the coefficients of ξ^♭ on K' continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), compose with the radial retraction of Λⁿ(ℝ^P) onto its closed unit ball for |·|, and multiply by a continuous χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V. The resulting continuous g has compact support in V, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere and g = ξ^♭ on K'. (d) Let g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise convolution with a standard mollifier). For 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V), g_ε is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫ φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)| dy ≤ 1 by convexity of the norm, and g_ε → g uniformly as ε → 0; so g_ε is admissible for M_W(T). (e) By steps 2 and 1, T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩| dμ_R − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K') − η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K) − 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) > t + 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄). As μ_R(V̄) < ∞, T(g_ε) > t for small ε. Together with step 3 this proves (i): M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
5. Support. By definition (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11) spt T = U ∖ Z, where Z is the union of all open W with W̄ compact, W̄ ⊆ U and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W. Recall x ∈ spt μ_R iff μ_R(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x. (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ_R and x ∈ Z, choose W in the union with x ∈ W; every admissible form for M_W(T) has T(ω) = 0, so M_W(T) = 0, hence μ_R(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ_R. So U ∩ spt μ_R ⊆ spt T. (b) spt T ⊆ U by definition. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ_R, choose r > 0 with μ_R(B_r(x)) = 0 and B̄_r(x) ⊆ U (U open). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R = 0 by step 2; so B_r(x) is one of the sets forming Z, x ∈ Z and x ∉ spt T. Hence spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R, which is (ii).
proof_key_steps: For a unit simple n-vector ξ, |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Binet), with equality for the dual covector ξ^♭.
T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R, so admissible forms give T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) arbitrarily close to μ_R(W).
The mass formula identifies the zero region of T with the complement of spt μ_R in U.

subproblems.title: The support of τ(M, θ, ξ) lies in every closed set containing M (parent step 4; Simon 6.2.11–2.12)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be a current in ℝ^P (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n) representing Y, i.e. Y(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). If F ⊆ ℝ^P is closed and M ⊆ F (R.carrier ⊆ F), then spt Y ⊆ F. Here spt Y = Y.support is Simon's support (6.2.11): ℝ^P minus the union of the relatively compact open sets W on which Y vanishes, i.e. Y(ω) = 0 whenever spt ω ⊆ W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (F : Set (Euclid P)), R.Represents Y → IsClosed F → R.carrier ⊆ F → Y.support ⊆ F
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof, which is Simon Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12 (chapter-06.txt lines 297–307: spt T = U ∖ ⋃W, and spt T = spt μ_T). The parent applies the lemma with F = L(spt X), a closed set containing the carrier N of the pushed-forward triple R'.
Sibling used: mass_support (dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support). For U open and R representing T in U, it gives spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R.
Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, H^n = μHE[n], μ_R = R.measure = θH^n⌞M (the measure H^n⌞M with density θ).
1. (μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ F) = 0.)
 - F is closed, so G := ℝ^P ∖ F is open, hence Borel.
 - By the definition of μ_R as a measure with density (withDensity_apply, then Measure.restrict_restrict): μ_R(G) = ∫_{G ∩ M} θ dH^n.
 - Since M ⊆ F, G ∩ M = ∅. The integral against the zero measure H^n⌞∅ vanishes (Measure.restrict_empty, lintegral_zero_measure).
 - So μ_R(G) = 0.
2. (An open null set misses the support.) G is open and μ_R(G) = 0 by step 1. Every point of G therefore has the neighbourhood G of μ_R-measure 0, so it does not lie in spt μ_R. Thus G ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ spt μ_R (Mathlib Measure.subset_compl_support_of_isOpen), i.e. spt μ_R ⊆ F.
3. (Conclusion.)
 - By mass_support with U = ℝ^P (open) and R representing Y: spt Y = ℝ^P ∩ spt μ_R = spt μ_R.
 - Let x ∈ spt Y. If x ∉ F, then x ∈ G ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ spt μ_R by step 2, contradicting x ∈ spt μ_R.
 - So x ∈ F, i.e. spt Y ⊆ F. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ F) = ∫_{(ℝ^P ∖ F) ∩ M} θ dH^n = 0, because M ⊆ F.
An open μ_R-null set is disjoint from spt μ_R, so spt μ_R ⊆ F.
spt Y = ℝ^P ∩ spt μ_R by sibling mass_support.

subproblems.title: A compactly carried integer multiplicity cycle annihilates every exact smooth form (cutoff step of Simon 6.2.23–2.24)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ. Let X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) be a current in ℝ^P (GeometricCurrentOn univ (k+1)), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ (k+1)) representing X, i.e. X(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dH^{k+1}(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^P). Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact with μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ K) = 0, where μ_R = θH^{k+1}⌞M (R.measure). If ∂X = 0 (X.boundary = 0), then R.action(dη) = ∫_M θ⟨dη, ξ⟩ dH^{k+1} = 0 for every smooth k-form η on ℝ^P (IsSmoothForm η: C^∞, with no support condition), where dη = exteriorDerivative η.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1)) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1)) (K : Set (Euclid P)) (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k), R.Represents X → IsCompact K → R.measure Kᶜ = 0 → X.boundary = 0 → IsSmoothForm η → R.action (exteriorDerivative η) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 5(b)–(e) of the parent proof. These are the cutoff argument of Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24 (chapter-06.txt lines 403–414): f_#T(ω) := T(ζ f^#ω) with ζ ≡ 1 near the compact set spt T ∩ spt f^#ω, "one easily checks that the definition … is independent of the particular choice of ζ", and ∂f_#T = f_#∂T. Here an arbitrary smooth form η plays the role of f^#ω, and the compact set K carrying μ_R plays the role of spt T. The parent applies the lemma with η = L^#φ and K = spt X.
No sibling is used.
Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, H^{k+1} = μHE[k + 1], μ_R = R.measure = θH^{k+1}⌞M (the measure H^{k+1}⌞M with density θ). For a form ω, dω = exteriorDerivative ω. This is Mathlib's extDeriv: dω(x) is the alternation of the derivative Dω(x).
1. (H^{k+1}(M ∖ K) = 0.)
 - K is compact, hence closed, so ℝ^P ∖ K is open and therefore Borel.
 - By the definition of μ_R as a measure with density (withDensity_apply, then Measure.restrict_restrict): μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ K) = ∫_{(ℝ^P ∖ K) ∩ M} θ dH^{k+1}.
 - θ is ℕ-valued and θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M (R.mult_pos), so θ ≥ 1 on M.
 - Hence H^{k+1}((ℝ^P ∖ K) ∩ M) = ∫_{(ℝ^P ∖ K) ∩ M} 1 dH^{k+1} ≤ ∫_{(ℝ^P ∖ K) ∩ M} θ dH^{k+1} = μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ K) = 0 (setLIntegral_one, setLIntegral_mono' on the measurable set (ℝ^P ∖ K) ∩ M).
 - Since M ∖ K = (ℝ^P ∖ K) ∩ M, H^{k+1}(M ∖ K) = 0.
 - Equivalently, H^{k+1}⌞M-a.e. point lies in K (ae_restrict_iff' with M measurable, ae_iff, measure_mono_null).
2. (The cutoff form.)
 - K is bounded, so K ⊆ B(0, r) for some r ∈ ℝ (Metric.isBounded_iff_subset_ball, from IsCompact.isBounded). Put ρ := max(r, 1). Then ρ > 0 and K ⊆ B(0, ρ).
 - Let ζ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] be the smooth bump function centred at 0 with inner radius ρ and outer radius ρ + 1 (Mathlib ContDiffBump with rIn = ρ, rOut = ρ + 1). It has three properties:
  * ζ is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff);
  * ζ = 1 on the closed ball B̄(0, ρ) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall);
  * ζ has compact support (ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport; ℝ^P is finite dimensional).
 - Define the k-form ψ by ψ(x) := ζ(x)·η(x). It is C^∞, as the product of the C^∞ function ζ and the C^∞ form η (ContDiff.smul). Take ContDiffBump.contDiff at order n = ⊤ in ℕ∞, which is the smoothness order ∞ of IsSmoothForm (not analyticity).
 - ψ has compact support because ζ does (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
 - So ψ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P): ψ with these two facts is a TestFormOn univ k, and tsupport ψ ⊆ ℝ^P is trivial.
 - Its exterior derivative is the test form exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k ψ ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^P), whose underlying form is dψ.
3. (dψ = dη on B(0, ρ).)
 - Let x ∈ B(0, ρ). The open ball B(0, ρ) is a neighbourhood of x.
 - For every y in that ball, y ∈ B̄(0, ρ), so ζ(y) = 1 and ψ(y) = 1·η(y) = η(y).
 - Thus ψ and η agree on a neighbourhood of x (ψ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] η).
 - dω(x) is computed from the derivative Dω(x), which depends only on the germ of ω at x. Hence dψ(x) = dη(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq).
4. (The two integrals agree.)
 - By step 1, H^{k+1}⌞M-a.e. x lies in K ⊆ B(0, ρ).
 - For such x, step 3 gives θ(x)·ξ(x)(dη(x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(dψ(x)).
 - So the integrands of R.action(dη) = ∫_M θ·ξ(dη) dH^{k+1} and R.action(dψ) = ∫_M θ·ξ(dψ) dH^{k+1} agree H^{k+1}⌞M-a.e. Hence R.action(dη) = R.action(dψ) (integral_congr_ae).
5. (∂X = 0 kills dψ.)
 - R represents X and dψ is a test form (step 2), so R.action(dψ) = X(dψ): apply R.Represents to exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k ψ.
 - By the definition of the boundary (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), X(dψ) = X(exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k ψ) = ∂X(ψ).
 - ∂X(ψ) = 0, since X.boundary = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply).
 - With step 4: R.action(dη) = R.action(dψ) = X(dψ) = ∂X(ψ) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: θ ≥ 1 on M turns μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ K) = 0 into H^{k+1}(M ∖ K) = 0, so H^{k+1}⌞M-a.e. point lies in K.
A bump function ζ ≡ 1 on B̄(0, ρ) ⊇ K makes ψ = ζη a compactly supported smooth k-form (a test form) with ψ = η on B(0, ρ).
The exterior derivative is local, so dψ = dη on B(0, ρ); hence R.action(dη) = R.action(dψ).
